doctrine: Reduce load before replacing plant: envelope and controls measures should be evaluated first so replacement equipment isn't oversized against a future-lower load
Boring-proven beats novel: packaged RTU replacement (gas/gas or heat-pump RTU where the electrical service supports it) beats an unproven exotic system a maintenance tech has never serviced
Right-size at replacement using the post-load-reduction Manual J/N-style estimate, not the nameplate of the unit being removed
Stage HVAC capital around equipment end-of-life and lease/capital events; don't replace working equipment to chase incremental efficiency unless the NOI math clears on its own
Measured baseline (utility bills, run-hours) governs savings claims; manufacturer AHRI ratings are inputs to a model, not proof of realized savings

Name tenant disruption honestly: RTU swaps on commercial roofs are typically none/light for tenants; in-unit PTAC or fan-coil replacement is in-unit disruption and may require vacancy scheduling for full-building conversions

Price the A2L refrigerant transition (AIM Act HFC phase-down) into any RTU/chiller replacement: post-2025 equipment uses mildly flammable A2L refrigerants (R-32, R-454B) with code, training, and cost implications — legacy R-410A units face rising service costs
origination_prompts: Any RTU or chiller nearing or past its ASHRAE-typical service life (RTUs ~15-20 yrs) in the PCA equipment schedule? Replacement-planning candidate.
Is the property in a climate and rate structure where a heat-pump RTU (or dual-fuel) pencils against a straight gas replacement?
Are units short-cycling, oversized, or mismatched to current occupancy per the audit's operating notes? Right-sizing candidate after load reduction.
Multiple failed compressors or refrigerant-leak service calls in maintenance logs => plant-level end-of-life signal, not a repair pattern.
feasibility_checks: Verify roof structural capacity and curb compatibility for any RTU swap, especially heat-pump RTUs which can be heavier
Check electrical service capacity before proposing electrified HVAC (heat-pump RTU, VRF) — this may require a panel/service upgrade measure first
Confirm crane access and staging area for rooftop equipment changeouts; tight urban sites raise cost and duration
Check Shovels for local mechanical contractors' HVAC permit volume as a market-capacity and pricing-reality signal
Name the tenant disruption class explicitly per unit type: none/light for central plant work, in-unit for terminal units, vacancy-required for full in-unit system conversions
Cold climates: verify heat-pump capacity derating at design temperature and specify backup/supplemental heat sizing before crediting full displacement
data_requirements: equipment inventory with install years and condition ratings
roof and electrical service capacity notes
